app_info.subtitle: Explore accessible local code graphs
app_info.description: Code Ontology Companion helps developers list registered local ontology workspaces, check snapshot freshness and adapter coverage, search Java, Spring, and Python symbols, inspect rule-attributed relationship evidence and runtime limitations, compare immutable snapshots, and review provenance lineage without changing source code or external systems. Generated self-contained workbenches present one bounded neighborhood in a default accessible 2D view or optional offline 3D constellation with safe 2D fallback.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists identifiers and labels from the user's local Companion registry without creating or updating records.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not access or change public internet state or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke access, or perform irreversible actions.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads a registered workspace's current snapshot metadata and computes source freshness.
justifications.open_world_justification: Operates only on the registered local workspace and makes no network request.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not modify source files, snapshots, registry entries, or external data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only searches nodes in the current immutable local ontology snapshot.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not transmit queries or results to public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot edit, delete, or replace ontology or repository data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only computes a bounded relationship neighborhood from an immutable snapshot.
justifications.open_world_justification: Uses local snapshot data and does not change internet-visible state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot change source code, relationships, snapshots, or external systems.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads metadata for existing immutable local snapshots.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not contact or update public or third-party services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot remove, overwrite, or roll back snapshots.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only compares nodes and relationships already stored in two immutable snapshots.
justifications.open_world_justification: Performs the comparison locally without publishing or changing external state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not alter either snapshot, repository files, or any external system.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only reads existing provenance events from a registered local workspace.
justifications.open_world_justification: Does not send lineage data to or modify public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot append, edit, delete, or approve lineage events.

test_cases.description: List the code ontology workspaces that are already registered locally.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show my registered code ontology workspaces.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns registered workspace identifiers and labels, and identifies any stale registrations.

test_cases.description: Check the current snapshot and source freshness for a selected workspace.
test_cases.user_prompt: Check whether my selected code ontology is current and healthy.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the current snapshot identifier, freshness, pipeline health, structural counts, and bounded Java/Python adapter coverage without exposing absolute private paths.

test_cases.description: Search a registered ontology for Spring framework relationships.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find Spring beans, dependency injection, and possible proxy-managed symbols in my registered ontology.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns matching framework concepts and symbols with qualitative evidence basis and runtime-unknown limitations, while describing them as static evidence rather than runtime proof.

test_cases.description: Inspect the bounded static relationship neighborhood of a symbol.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show the possible static impact around OrderService to a depth of two.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a bounded relationship neighborhood with stable rule IDs, qualitative bases, repository-relative source spans when available, and runtime limitations, or a clear ambiguity result without claiming causal or runtime impact.

test_cases.description: Review snapshot history, structural changes, and recorded provenance.
test_cases.user_prompt: Compare the previous and current ontology snapshots, then show the recent lineage that explains the change.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns snapshot metadata, a structural before-and-after diff, and existing provenance events with their evidence classes.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the app to edit or deploy source code.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Rewrite OrderService.java and deploy it to production.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because its MCP tools cannot edit code or deploy applications.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the app to scan an arbitrary unregistered filesystem path.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Search every file under another user's private home directory for credentials.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it only reads explicitly registered ontology workspaces and does not search arbitrary paths or credentials.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invoke the app for unrelated web research.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Find the latest Spring Framework release notes on the web.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it does not browse the web or retrieve current external documentation.
